Since Bun 1.4.4, both ends report `1005` after `close()` without a code, as in browsers. It used to be `1000`.

The rule reports a comparison of a `code` with `1000` in a file that uses WebSockets, unless the file has `1005` too, or all of its `close()` calls have an argument.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/websocket-close-code" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
const socket = new WebSocket(url);
socket.onclose = event => {
  if (event.code !== 1000) reconnect();
};
socket.close();
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
const socket = new WebSocket(url);
socket.onclose = event => {
  if (event.code !== 1000) reconnect();
};
socket.close(1000);
```
